name: k_core
author: 3f28ff34
description: Finds the tightly connected core of a graph by k-core decomposition: repeatedly removes nodes with fewer than k connections until every remaining node has at least k neighbours inside the core. Use it for questions like 'what is the tightly connected core', 'which nodes are most deeply embedded', or 'which group has everyone linked to at least 5 others'. Leave k out to get the densest core (the largest k with a non-empty core). Works on all graphs; on directed graphs a node's connections are its incoming plus outgoing edges, and edge weights are ignored. Returns k, max_core_number, size (the number of nodes in the core), the top_k core nodes by core number with id, label and core_number, and result_graph_id: the core as a subgraph that other tools can run on next.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

k.description: Minimum number of connections each node must have inside the core. Leave it out to get the densest core.

top_k.description: How many core nodes to list, highest core number first. size and result_graph_id always cover the whole core.
